To bring it back, sign in to the **Manus account that owns the project** and go to [Data Backup](https://manus.im/backup). Then restore the **Task Data Backup** containing this website. For a Type A/B affected account, restore the task-data package directly. For a Type C account, restore the account first, then restore the task-data package. Upload **all** correct, most-recent backup packages together—restoration is a one-time action. [1]

| Situation | Required action | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| You have the site’s Task Data Backup | Restore it at `manus.im/backup` | A previously deployed site is redeployed automatically, including its default `manus.space` address. [1] |

| No Task Data Backup exists | The affected site, database, uploaded files, and configuration cannot be restored from source code alone | Contact Manus support for account-specific assistance. [2] |

You do **not** need to recreate the database or run migrations after a successful restore. If the website was live before the backup, restoring returns it to the backup’s snapshot, including the code, files, database, configuration, and secrets. Third-party integrations/connectors may need to be manually re-enabled afterward. [1]

If you can tell me whether you have the backup package (and whether the project was previously published), I can guide you through the exact next screen.
